title: Mount Etna Ash Forces Extended Closure of Sicilys Catania Airport
excerpt: Fresh volcanic ash emissions from Europes most active volcano have suspended all flights at Italys fifth-busiest airport during peak summer travel season, stranding tourists across Sicily and Malta.
body:
• Catania airport suspended all arrivals and departures until at least 1600 GMT on Wednesday as Mount Etna continued emitting volcanic ash over eastern Sicily.
  • The disruption extended beyond Sicily, with flight cancellations and delays reported in neighbouring Malta as ash drifted across the Mediterranean.
  • Palermo airport absorbed 190 diverted flights in recent days, but stranded passengers reported inadequate ground transportation assistance.
  • Travel disruptions have persisted since last week, placing severe pressure on Sicilys smaller airports during one of the busiest tourist periods of the year.

Eruption Extends Airspace Restrictions

Flights at Sicilys Catania airport were suspended again on Wednesday as fresh ash emissions from Mount Etna forced Italian aviation authorities to extend airspace restrictions around eastern Sicily. Airport operator SAC confirmed that all arrivals and departures would remain grounded until at least 1600 GMT.

Passengers are advised to check the status of their flights with their airlines. Further updates will follow in the coming hours, SAC said in a statement.

Mount Etna, Europes highest and most active volcano at 3,330 metres, has been in a state of heightened volcanic activity for over a week. Renewed eruptions and shifting winds began carrying ash across the region last week, disrupting operations at Catania — Sicilys main gateway and Italys fifth-busiest airport by passenger traffic.

Impact Spreads Across the Mediterranean

The latest eruption extended its reach beyond Sicily. Flight cancellations and significant delays were reported overnight in neighbouring Malta as volcanic ash drifted south across the Mediterranean. While conditions appeared to improve on Wednesday, Malta International Airport continued to warn passengers of possible disruptions.

The prolonged restrictions at Catania have placed additional pressure on Sicilys other airports during peak summer season. Airlines including Ryanair, easyJet, Wizz Air, ITA Airways, Delta, Lufthansa, and Norwegian Air have all been forced to cancel or divert flights.

Palermo Airport Absorbs Overflow

Palermo Mayor Roberto Lagalla said the citys airport had absorbed 190 flights originally scheduled to arrive at or depart from Catania in recent days. However, the surge in diverted traffic created its own problems.

"Passengers are advised to check the status of their flights with their airlines. Further updates will follow in the coming hours."

— SAC, Catania airport operator

Some passengers rerouted to Palermo complained of inadequate assistance with onward transportation, as demand for buses and taxis surged following their arrival. Extra traffic caused delays at Palermo airport as well, operators said.

Comiso airport, a smaller facility south of Catania that has also been used to absorb overflow traffic, returned to full operations on Wednesday after suspending flights on Tuesday evening due to ash from Mount Etna, Italian news agency ANSA reported.

A Familiar Pattern for Catania

Mount Etna frequently disrupts operations at Catania airport, which attracts more arrivals than Palermo and serves as a critical gateway for tourists visiting eastern Sicily. The volcano entered a renewed eruptive phase earlier this month, producing significant ash emissions and lava flows from the Voragine summit crater.

Italys National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology raised the Volcano Observatory Notice for Aviation to red during the most intense phase of activity, though the alert has since been downgraded. Travel insurers have noted that coverage for volcanic ash disruption varies by policy, with many providing benefits when flights are cancelled due to unforeseen natural events.

Sicilys regional government has arranged onward transport for affected passengers arriving at alternative airports as the disruption continues.
